front: How do you classify agent actions for autonomy?
back: By operational, security and compliance risk (and reversibility); assign the lowest safe level of human involvement.
Maximize delivery speed while remaining compliant with security and Responsible AI standards.

front: Which actions always need explicit authorization or a controlled path?
back: Irreversible or compliance-sensitive ones: production deploys, data deletion, secrets and permission changes.
Instructions are advisory; allowlists, firewall, rulesets, required checks and hooks cannot be bypassed by the model.
Tool allowlists, firewall, rulesets/branch protection, required reviews/CODEOWNERS, push protection/code scanning, org policies, hooks.
Read-only tools and endpoints, fine-grained PAT or GitHub App scoped to specific repos, narrow tools list.

front: How do you preserve velocity with guardrails?
back: Risk-based approvals at PR level, async review, auto-allow read-only actions, no approvals that do not reduce risk.
Users with write access. Comments from users without write access are never shown to it.
Draft PRs need human review and merge; agent cannot mark ready, approve or merge; requester cannot approve.
PRs opened under the agent's own identity need one additional approval if the repo already requires approvals (ruleset default; always for branch protection).
Do not run until a user with write access clicks Approve and run workflows (configurable).

front: Prompt-injection mitigation built into cloud agent?
back: Hidden characters filtered (for example HTML comments are not passed); non-write users' comments excluded.
Restricted internet access via the firewall (customizable allowlist).
Copilot as author, requester as co-author, signed (Verified), link to session logs; admin audit log events.
Attributed to creator, you choose exactly which tools it can use, untrusted-user events ignored by default, workflows still need human approval.
Ambiguity, business/ethical trade-offs, security-sensitive and irreversible changes.

front: How do you gate a production deploy by an agent?
back: Protected environment with required reviewers (explicit authorization), plus protected branch and checks.

front: Why is 'approve every tool call' bad?
back: It adds friction without materially reducing risk; the exam favors risk-proportional controls.

front: Who is accountable for merged agent code?
back: Humans: reviewers and the team. 'The agent did it' is not a control.
